site: Philae, Gate of Hadrian: outer face of the west wall, south of the gateway, a little north of no. 122 and higher up

text_corpus: tewisti pelmoSl yetmde apote yeSo dilXe tbo woS pileqetel woS tebwetel nbetw yeberwi yiwriyipno woS mkdilX kSbN woS sbto
notes: 7 stone lines; superscripts (2)-(7) printed. Printed only in the Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae (p. 50), assembled from its rows in section order: A (the right column tewiseti, then the left part), B, C (right part, then left part), E; section D has no row for 123 (its lines numbered 7 to 10 belong to 122). Griffith's queries: '?' over the ẖ and the e of di(3)lẖe; 'sic' over the e after l in pileqete(4)l. His note (p. 48): all is clear on the squeezes 'except the sign' e '(?) at the beginning of l. 3, which might possibly be' a 3-shaped sign (m/ẖ) or w, 'or even an accidental cutting'; in the table the superscript 3 stands before l of lẖe. A crack runs through the first six lines near the right-hand edges. His English (p. 52): 'The adoration made by (?) the kin of the strategus, the envoy, zilake-tabê, remaining (?) before Isis in Philae, Isis in Tebawe ....... Isis the great goddess (?), belonging to the kashbañs of Isis.' He compares tbo with 101/11 and di?e with 64; 122 and 123 end in the same three words (ksbñ wos sebto; 122 prints dividers between them). A line number set between signs leaves no word space of its own in the type (16-20 px before it and 36-39 px after it, the same at every number), so words meeting at a line number are written joined, as printed. So di(3)lẖe, nbe(5)tw and yiwri(6)yipno are joined; yiwri and yipno may be two words. 3-shaped signs decided at 3-5x beside the sure m of pelmosl and ye(2)tmde (round top) and the closed s of yeso and ksbñ: ẖ (angular top, pointed middle) in di(3)lẖe and in mkdilẖ, which a first look at 2.5x had read ?kdils; p (left-pointing vertices, as in apote), not k, in yipno. No sign left uncertain by me. ' | ' separates the rows of Griffith's table (its sections A, B, C, E) that hold this text, right part before left part within a row; (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign; [...] his dots.

notes: 4 stone lines; superscripts (2)-(4) printed. Printed only in the Table of Seven Graffiti of Philae (p. 50), assembled from its rows A, B and C, with 'end' after C. Griffith's queries: '?' over the a of aso; 'sic' over the divider in te : (4)bwetele, which splits Tebawe. His English (p. 52): 'The adoration made by (?) Pkhêpe, nakharezas keñayze of the khabkheñ in Zaq, worshipping (?) Harendotes in Tebawe.' His notes (p. 51): arette is Aretate, the god Harendotes (Hr-nt-yt-f); dqtele (125/2) is a place-name, 'in Zaq', its appendage spelt as in te : bwetele (125/3-4); aḫrlo, 'worshipper' (?), replaces the usual words of piety. The type has keñydi, final i (the i of tewiseti), where his English has keñayze. A tiny speck after q in dqtele is not a divider. A line number set between signs leaves no word space of its own in the type (16-20 px before it and 36-39 px after it, the same at every number), so words meeting at a line number are written joined, as printed. ẖ in pẖope decided at 3x (angular top, pointed middle, against the round-topped m of 123), and Griffith renders it kh (Pkhêpe); k (right-pointing vertices) in keñydi. No sign left uncertain by me. ' | ' separates the rows of Griffith's table (its sections A, B, C, E) that hold this text, right part before left part within a row; (n) is his superscript stone-line number, kept where printed; [x] his restoration; [.] a lost sign; [...] his dots.
